fact: Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN) partnered in May 2023 to develop Project East2West, a roughly US$320m terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to east and west coast subsea cables, and the document names South Sudan among the countries covered.

South Sudan's ICT ministry invited international bids (SS-MICT&PS-544330-NC-RFB, bids closing 26 October 2026) for about 397 km of terrestrial fibre on the Juba-Nadapal route toward the Kenyan border, financed under World Bank grant E1780 of the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project; this is procurement, not yet works, and the notice date is given as the report's 2026-09-14 publication.

South Sudan granted Bayobab Infra Solutions a 15-year licence in October 2025 to build and operate national and cross-border fibre networks, international leased circuits and IP transit, as part of Project East 2 West, a fibre corridor connecting East and West Africa.

The World Bank's June 2026 status report on the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project lists as a key achievement the signing of the first cross-border digital connectivity MoU between Kenya and South Sudan, a model for the remaining bilateral MoUs; the signing date is not given, so the report's published date is used.
